name: RubicProxy routerCallNative executes an arbitrary whitelisted call
summary: RubicProxy.routerCallNative() forwards caller-supplied calldata to a caller-supplied router address, checking only that the router is in availableRouters. The contract makes no distinction between a swap router and an ERC-20, so once USDC was added to that list any caller could pass USDC as the router and transferFrom(victim, attacker, amount) as the calldata, spending the unlimited approvals users had granted the proxy.
notes: Non-upgradeable contract despite the name. The runtime code hash is 0xf85cac648771ec2734fad7a38d82ea27a63265046c9d58293c472b0209dbaa75 both at the deployment block 15395828 and at block 16260580, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so no code change occurred between deployment and the exploit.

The exploiter’s two transactions, at blocks 16260581 and 16260623, pull 1508457.385172 USDC from 49 distinct approval-holding addresses into the exploit contract 0x253dd81d642220267ccac1d8202c0b96a92b299e. Four further transactions in the same fifteen minutes drive the same defect from other senders against other collector contracts; several are consistent with whitehat rescue rather than theft, so they are not counted here and their amounts are not in this figure. Losses fall on individual approval holders, not on protocol-held funds. DefiLlama prices USDC at 1.00033 at the incident timestamp, so par is marginally conservative. Nothing was recovered by the protocol itself.

Four further transactions at blocks 16260953, 16260999, 16261017 and 16261025 exercise the same defect from other senders against other collector contracts and are excluded from the loss because several are consistent with whitehat rescue.
